findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data will throw
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma updateMany requires at least one field to update; an empty data object throws a validation error. This runs after every successful cache population, so watching/subscribing a calendar will fail after the cache write. If the intent is to bump updatedAt, pass { updatedAt: new Date() } explicitly.

findings.title: Unfiltered credentialIds can break cache status query
findings.body: credentialIds is built as connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId) with no filtering. Delegation or in-memory credentials can have undefined/null/negative credentialIds, and a user with no calendars yields an empty array. Passing those values to prisma.calendarCache.groupBy where credentialId: { in: credentialIds } can throw or return wrong results, breaking the whole connectedCalendars query. Filter to finite positive numbers and early-return when empty.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache rows
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows by credentialId with no expiresAt filter, while getCachedAvailability only honors rows with expiresAt >= now. After expiry the UI will still show a Last updated timestamp and offer Delete cached data for data that will never be used. Add the same expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } filter used elsewhere.

findings.title: Cache delete never refreshes cache status UI
findings.body: deleteCacheMutation onSuccess only shows a toast and calls onSuccess, but unlike disconnectMutation it never invalidates trpc.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The cacheUpdatedAt timestamp fetched by connectedCalendarsHandler therefore stays stale after deletion and the dropdown still shows the old Last updated time until a manual reload.

findings.title: Helper script uses macOS-only sed and fragile relative path
findings.body: The script writes with ENV_FILE="../.env" relative to the current working directory, so running from anywhere except scripts/ clobbers the wrong file. It also uses sed -i '' -E which only works on macOS BSD sed and fails on Linux/GNU sed. Committing it as-is breaks Linux developers and CI.
